The '''stream of consciousness''' is a literary technique seeking to represent the disorganisation, repetition inherent to natural human thought.

== History ==

The term stream of consciousness was first used by psychologists to describe the human thought process. Its use as a literary technique became popular in the 20th century as part of the [[Modernist movement]].<ref>{{#cite:Q1963}}</ref>

== Characteristics ==

The use of stream of consciousness is often associated with:

* Unconventional ponctuation, such as mid-sentence interruption;
* Improper capitalisation;
* Unconventional grammatical structure
<ref>{{#cite:Q1963}}</ref>
